data.current_summary: Refresh a person or retrieve public LinkedIn data
data.current_description: Set type=refresh and provide a LinkedIn profile URL for current public details at the response root. Person/profile returns a profile object; company a company object; posts and people/search arrays; a job URL returns one record under jobs while job searches return an array. Field availability varies. Each successful operation uses its endpoint rate; enriched People is billed per full profile and Refresh per accessible profile. Empty and failed results are uncharged. Missing values or URL status do not prove a job change or permanent deletion.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve or refresh LinkedIn profile, company, or job data
data.description_suggestion: Fetches public LinkedIn data by type: use type=refresh for current profile details, type=person/profile for profile objects, type=company for company objects, type=posts for post arrays, type=people/search for people search results, or provide a job URL to retrieve job records. Returns data at the response root with structure varying by type (single objects for profile/company, arrays for posts/people/search, single job record for URL or array for searches). Field availability varies by record. Billing: Refresh charges per accessible profile, enriched People per full profile, other types per successful request. Empty results and failures are free. Note: Missing values or URL status changes do not indicate job changes or permanent deletions.

data.current_description: Up to 100 URLs synchronously, or 10,000 with a public HTTPS webhook. Supported types: refresh, person/profile, company, posts. Results remain in input order. Each row carries its own data or error and successful rows use the chosen endpoint rate. Large webhook payloads may be replaced by a temporary resultsUrl; download before resultsExpireAt. Status requests return counts and delivery state, not result rows. Webhooks cannot contain embedded credentials; redirects are not followed and failed delivery is retried once.
data.description_suggestion: Batch process up to 100 LinkedIn URLs synchronously or 10,000 asynchronously via webhook. Supported types: refresh, person/profile, company, posts. Provide URLs in request body; results maintain input order with each row containing either data or error. Successful rows are billed at the chosen endpoint rate; failed rows are free. For synchronous requests, returns results directly. For asynchronous requests with webhook: large payloads are stored at a temporary resultsUrl (download before resultsExpireAt); webhooks cannot contain embedded credentials, redirects are not followed, and failed delivery is retried once. Use GET with batch_id to check status (returns counts and delivery state, not result rows).

data.current_description: One endpoint for the whole Google menu. Set `type` to choose the surface (default `web`). Each type returns a JSON response under its own key: web/scholar/patents/lens -> `organic`; news -> `news`; shopping -> `shopping`; images -> `images`; videos -> `videos`; maps/places -> `places`; reviews -> `reviews`; autocomplete -> `suggestions`; webpage -> `text` + `metadata` + `jsonld`. Google surfaces are billed per successful request at the Google Search rate, except type=maps, which bills per business returned at the Maps rate. Wallet prices depend on the available funds and their saved rates. Failed and empty results are free. Legacy credit accounts retain their existing billing model.
data.summary_suggestion: Search Google surfaces (web, maps, news, images, videos, shopping, reviews, scholar, patents, autocomplete)
data.description_suggestion: Unified endpoint for querying multiple Google search surfaces. Specify the search type via the `type` parameter (default: web). Supported types: web, maps, places, news, shopping, images, videos, reviews, scholar, patents, autocomplete, and webpage. Each type returns results under a specific key: web/scholar/patents/lens return `organic`, news returns `news`, shopping returns `shopping`, images return `images`, videos return `videos`, maps/places return `places`, reviews return `reviews`, autocomplete returns `suggestions`, and webpage returns `text`, `metadata`, and `jsonld`.
